issues.title: Lebesgue-measure cover algorithm
issues.failure_explanation: For fixed n and A, the cover consists of the disjoint intervals [a_{m,n}(A),b_{m,n}(A)], so its measure is the sum of their lengths. The old expression computes the sum of the right endpoints followed by one free-indexed subtraction, rather than summing b_{m,n}(A)-a_{m,n}(A), and therefore does not define the claimed scalar output as written.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed Lebesgue-measure algorithm is malformed, leaving the Lebesgue-measure branches of the (S1) and (S2) classification corollaries unsupported until corrected. Their other branches are unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the output by Γ_n(A) = Σ_{m=1}^{M_n(A)}(b_{m,n}(A) − a_{m,n}(A)) and use this scalar in the Lebesgue-measure branches of the two listed corollaries. No other proof or statement needs alteration.
issues.why_classification: The disjoint-interval cover and the stated goal of computing its Lebesgue measure uniquely force the sum of the interval lengths. The free-indexed subtraction is a transcriptional summand/parenthesization error; correcting it requires no mathematical inference and preserves all affected guarantees.

issues.title: Box-counting tower's incorrect inner-limit identity
issues.failure_explanation: For fixed n_2, taking n_1 to infinity in the maximum of a_{k,n_1} yields the supremum of the ratios involving N_{\delta_k}(\Gamma_{n(\delta_k)}^\spec(A)). The old proof replaced these sets by the exact spectrum. The preceding estimate only bounds the cover count within a factor of three and does not give equality for fixed k or fixed n_2. Although the two sequences have the same outer limsup, the displayed inner-limit equality is invalid.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the proof of the upper box-counting Pi_2 classification contains an unsupported equality. The theorem is recoverable locally; later formal results either use the valid factor-three estimate or provide an independent upper-box argument rather than relying on this defective fixed-n_2 identity.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the fixed-n₂ inner-limit identity by the supremum of log(N_{δ_k}(Γ_{n(δ_k)}^spec(A)))/log(1/δ_k) over k ≥ n₂. Then use the already established factor-three covering estimate, or the preceding limsup identity, to identify the outer limit with the upper box-counting dimension.
issues.why_classification: The definition of a_{k,j} directly yields the corrected cover-based supremum, while equality with the exact-spectrum expression need not hold at fixed k. This is an invalid proof inference rather than a transcriptional typo, but its repair is short and routine and preserves the theorem and its SCI classification without new machinery or weakening.

issues.title: Graph-layer construction assumes un stated local finiteness

failure_location.quote: Starting with $v_1$, we list its neighbors as $S_1=\{v_1,\ldots,v_{q_1}\}$ for some finite $q_1$.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Consider a connected, undirected graph $\mathcal{G}$ such that the set of vertices $\mathcal{V}=\mathcal{V}(\mathcal{G})$ is countably infinite.
For simplicity, assume that for any $v\in \mathcal{V}$, the set of vertices $w$ with $\alpha(v,w)\neq 0$ or $\alpha(w,v)\neq 0$ is finite.

issues.failure_explanation: The finite-support assumption on alpha restricts operator couplings, not the number of graph edges. For example, take a countably infinite star graph rooted at v_1 and the zero bounded self-adjoint operator. All old alpha- and S-assumptions hold, but v_1 has infinitely many graph neighbors, so there is no finite q_1 and the stated finite-layer breadth-first procedure cannot begin.
issues.overall_effect: The breadth-first construction is not executable for every graph admitted by the example. The general bounded-dispersion theorem is unaffected, and the example's principal membership conclusion can still be obtained directly from the already assumed support function S.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain the original graph class and replace the universally asserted finite graph-neighbor construction by the direct support-based choice f(n) = max{n+1,S(1),…,S(n)}. The assumed property of S then gives D_{f,n}(A)=0. Present the breadth-first layers and lattice-growth estimates only as an additional construction for locally finite graphs.
issues.why_classification: The omitted local-finiteness premise is a genuine defect, so this is not a typo. Nevertheless, the already assumed support function S supplies a short, routine, complete bypass that preserves the original graph class, the construction of a suitable f, and the bounded-dispersion conclusion; the breadth-first illustration remains valid in its intended locally finite setting.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: the set of vertices $\mathcal{V}=\mathcal{V}(\mathcal{G})$ is countably infinite and any vertex has only finitely many edges.

issues.title: Penrose graph-model attribution
issues.failure_explanation: The old caption claims that the 76-node, 135-edge graph is T_2. The same caption says the three displayed models are T_1, T_2, and T_3 in sequence and already assigns T_2 76 nodes and 205 edges. Thus the last count belongs to the third displayed model, T_3; the old wording attributes it to the wrong model.
issues.overall_effect: The local graph-size data are attached to the wrong Penrose model in the caption. No theorem, algorithm, or later formal result depends on the erroneous subscript.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the final model label in the caption from T₂ to T₃, retaining the count of 76 nodes and 135 edges.
issues.why_classification: The caption identifies the three displayed graphs as T₁, T₂, and T₃ in order and has already assigned the other 76-node count to T₂. Thus the old source uniquely forces the final subscript T₃; this is a local transcription error with no dependent mathematics.

issues.title: Fibonacci-dimension conjecture operand

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We conjecture that the box-counting and Hausdorff dimensions of the spectrum of the $d$-dimensional Fibonacci Hamiltonian are equal and satisfy
Let $F\subset\mathbb{R}$ be bounded and $N_\delta(F)$ denote the number of $\delta$-mesh intervals that intersect $F$.

issues.failure_explanation: The rightmost term literally applies box-counting dimension to the operator H_lambda, although the supplied definition takes a bounded set F as its operand. The conjecture explicitly concerns dimensions of spectra and its two left-hand terms both use spec(H_lambda^(d)), so the intended right-hand operand is spec(H_lambda).
issues.overall_effect: The labeled conjectural identity is ill-typed as written. Its intended spectral-dimension formula and the following conjectural asymptotic become well-defined after inserting spec; no proved formal result is affected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the rightmost operand dim_B(H_λ) by dim_B(spec(H_λ)), so the term reads min{1,d·dim_B(spec(H_λ))}. No proved result requires modification.
issues.why_classification: The supplied definition applies box-counting dimension to bounded sets, while the surrounding sentence and both left-hand terms explicitly concern spectra. The old source therefore uniquely forces insertion of spec; this is an ill-typed omitted operand wrapper rather than a defect in the conjectural reasoning.
